LMDI decomposition of a count over the factors of a Kaya identity

Source: R/envc.R
lmdix.Rd

How much of a change in recorded environmental offences (pollution cases, waste violations) between two years, or of a region's gap to a reference region, is owed to each factor of an identity that multiplies out to the count: the additive log-mean Divisia index (LMDI) decomposition, temporal and spatial, as Duan et al. (2026, eqs 1-5, pp. 8-9) apply it to crimes of polluting the environment in 30 Chinese provinces, 2016-2023.

Usage

lmdix(
  y,
  q,
  unit,
  time,
  type = "time",
  at = NULL,
  ref = "mean",
  zero = 0,
  fnm = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'lmdix'
plot(x, ..., main = NULL, col = NULL, pal = NULL, units = NULL)

Arguments

y

The count of each row (a unit in a period): numbers from 0.

q

The quantities of the chain, in order: a numeric matrix or data frame with one row per row of y and one column per quantity, numbers from 0; the column names name the factors.

unit

The unit of each row: labels.

time

The period of each row: numbers; each unit at most once per period.

type

"time" (change between periods) or "space" (gap to the reference region of each period).

at

NULL or the periods to use, increasing: for "time", the end points of consecutive intervals (default the first and last period; Duan et al. used 2016, 2018, 2020 and 2023); for "space", the periods to decompose (default all).

ref

"mean" or "gmean": the reference region of "space".

zero

0 (rows with a zero get NA) or a positive number put in place of the zeros.

fnm

NULL or the names of the ncol(q) + 1 factors.

x

An lmdix result.

...

Passed to the base-graphics call.

main

NULL (a default title) or one string.

col

NULL (the palette) or colours.

pal

NULL (the session palette, see plotopt()) or a palette name for blpal().

units

NULL (every unit) or the units whose rows are summed.

Value

An object of class lmdix, a list: dec, one row per unit and interval (unit, from, to, y0, y1, dy) or per unit and period (unit, time, ref the reference count, y, dy), followed by one column of contributions per factor; fac, the count and the factor values of every row (unit, time, y, one column per factor); ref, for "space", the reference region's count and factors by period, else NULL; factors, the factor names; type; and refkind.

Details

The identity is built as a chain from the quantities q_1, ..., q_m (the columns of q, in order): y = (y / q_1) (q_1 / q_2) ... (q_{m-1} / q_m) q_m, m + 1 factors that multiply to y whatever the quantities. Duan et al.'s eq 1 is the chain of population P, area S, emissions W, GDP, population again and the unemployed UN: CPEs = CPER x PD x EIPA^-1 x PEI x EDL x UR^-1 x UN, the case rate per head, population density, area per unit of emission, emission per unit of GDP, GDP per head, people per unemployed person and the unemployed (see the example). The factor values themselves, the rates of the identity, are returned in fac.

With type = "time" the change of each unit between consecutive periods of at is y_T - y_O = sum_j L(y_T, y_O) ln(f_jT / f_jO) (eqs 2-3), L(a, b) = (a - b) / (ln a - ln b) the logarithmic mean; a unit missing either period is left out. With type = "space" each unit of each period in at is set against a reference region of the same period (eqs 4-5): with ref = "mean", the region whose count and quantities are the means over the units present, so its count is the average count Duan et al. benchmark against; with ref = "gmean", the geometric means. Duan et al. do not say how the reference region's factors were formed; the arithmetic means of the quantities are this function's reading of "the national average", and "gmean" the alternative. The decomposition has no residual: the contributions add up to dy.

A zero count or quantity has no logarithm. With zero = 0 (Duan et al.'s "Null: no numerical value", figs 5-6) the rows it touches get NA contributions; with zero positive, zeros are replaced by it first. The contributions then depend on zero, and only slowly fade as it shrinks (as one over its logarithm), so a replaced zero should be reported as such.

The plot draws the contribution of each factor summed over the rows (of units), as horizontal bars, and returns those sums.

Environmental crime

The family treats offences against the environment as the outcome: where, when and why pollution offences, illegal waste disposal and trafficking, and safety crimes in extractive industries are recorded, and how enforcement behaves. Its tools are lmdix() (decomposition over a Kaya identity, Duan et al. 2026), fepnl() (two-way fixed effects with an interaction and the checks Duan et al. report) and pcdtst() (cross-sectional dependence of a panel, Andreatta et al. 2023), gmmpnl() (difference and system GMM for dynamic panels, as Andreatta et al. fit them), wsctst() (Wooldridge's test of serial correlation) and ccepnl() (common correlated effects), with the package's spatial tests (gmoran(), gearc(), lmorn()) for the spatial checks Andreatta et al. run. Recorded counts are counts of detected, prosecuted or judged cases: Duan et al. count first-instance judgments, Andreatta et al. the violations verified by law enforcement and gathered by an NGO, and both say the counts carry enforcement as well as offending (Andreatta et al. write the observed rate as the true rate plus a measurement error that can move with enforcement, p. 1372). Safety crimes are "violations of law by employers that either do, or have the potential to, cause sudden death or injury as a result of work-related activities" (Tombs and Whyte, quoted by Pitoulis 2014, p. 2); they are mostly regulatory offences enforced by inspectorates rather than police, mostly end in guilty pleas and fines (p. 47), and the injuries behind them are under-reported (p. 3, note 1), so recorded counts understate them. None of the three sources specifies a model of recorded against true offences, and the family has none.

References

Duan, H., Nie, C., He, B., Chen, X., Duan, Z., Chen, S., Song, J. and Gao, Z. (2026). A multi-method framework for decoding the spatiotemporal patterns and driving factors of environmental pollution crimes in China. Humanities and Social Sciences Communications. doi:10.1057/s41599-026-08766-9

Andreatta, D., Favarin, S., Lisciandra, M. and Millemaci, E. (2023). Digging into waste: an analysis of waste crime in the Italian provinces. Regional Studies, 57(7), 1367-1379. doi:10.1080/00343404.2022.2135697

Pitoulis, T. T. (2014). Bloody Oil: A Critical Discourse Analysis of Safety Crimes in the Alberta Oil and Gas Industry. MA thesis in criminology, University of Ottawa.

Examples

# six provinces over four years: cases, population (millions), area
# (1000 km2), emissions (1000 t), GDP (billions) and the unemployed
# (millions), simulated
set.seed(1)
d <- expand.grid(year = c(2016, 2018, 2020, 2023), prov = LETTERS[1:6])
i <- match(d$prov, LETTERS)
d$P <- 10 * i * (1 + 0.01 * (d$year - 2016))
d$S <- 50 + 20 * i
d$W <- 30 * i * (1 - 0.03 * (d$year - 2016))
d$GDP <- 40 * i * (1 + 0.05 * (d$year - 2016))
d$UN <- 0.3 * i * (1 + 0.02 * (d$year - 2016))
d$cases <- rpois(24, 2 * i + 8 * (d$year == 2018))
q <- d[c("P", "S", "W", "GDP", "P", "UN")]
f <- c("CPER", "PD", "EIPA^-1", "PEI", "EDL", "UR^-1", "UN")
r <- lmdix(d$cases, q, d$prov, d$year, at = c(2016, 2018, 2020, 2023),
           fnm = f)
r
#> lmdix: time decomposition, 18 rows, 7 factors
#> contributions summed over the rows decomposed:
#>         dy       CPER         PD    EIPA^-1        PEI        EDL      UR^-1 
#>   1.000000  -2.821646   3.821646  13.156108 -30.253445  13.275691  -3.597145 
#>         UN 
#>   7.418791 
# the gap of each province to the average province, by year
lmdix(d$cases, q, d$prov, d$year, type = "space", fnm = f)$dec
